headline: Maui Police Commission

meeting.summary: In closed session, the Maui Police Commission voted to suggest unpaid leave for a lieutenant and approved hiring an investigator.
meeting.recap: The commission received 17 written testimonies on agenda item 6A.[[0:01:59]] Eight juveniles were arrested for riot in that case.[[0:10:15]] The case was referred to the FBI for possible hate crime implications.[[0:10:28]] The department gave back over $5 million in unspent salary money at the end of the fiscal year.[[0:20:35]] As of August 12, 44 police applicants were in the hiring process.[[0:31:47]] The commission voted 8 to 1 to go into executive session (a closed-door discussion).[[0:47:29]] In closed session, the commission voted to suggest that a lieutenant be put on administrative leave without pay.[[0:49:29]] The commission voted 7 to 0 to hire an investigator.[[0:49:53]] The investigation will look at oversight of the police criminal intelligence unit.[[0:50:12]] It will also look at how the chief responded when he learned of the unit's issues.[[0:51:03]] The commission voted 5 to 2 to hire a commission investigator recommended by one of its working groups.[[0:51:24]]
decided: A letter of commendation for a police officer was filed without objection.
The commission voted to suggest that a lieutenant be put on administrative leave without pay.
The commission approved hiring an investigator, with a scope to be outlined by corporation counsel.
The commission voted to accept a working group's recommendation on who to hire as commission investigator.
meeting.next: The commission will bring its unpaid leave suggestion to the administration. The chief agreed to provide more statistics, including month-to-date, year-to-date and year-over-year comparisons.
